- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.5) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.5) — model tends to ignore downside risk; add buffer to forecast if sentiment is persistently negative.
- Lagged price movements are often over-predicted in early forecast windows — model reacts too slowly to sentiment shifts; apply a 1–2 day lag correction for sentiment-driven reversals.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes — model tends to overreact; cap forecast peaks at 1.2x recent high or 1.5x 14-day moving average.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.5 standard deviations above recent mean, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Sentiment reversal triggers mean reversion: if sentiment drops sharply after a peak, reduce forecast by 5–15% for next 3–5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to over-optimism — apply 5–10% downward adjustment if sentiment is weak or volatile in last 7 days.
